identifiers: RX1 has 'RX1' on the front; RX1R adds an 'R'. Same body; the RX1R has no AA filter.

viewfinder.note: None built in; hot-shoe EVF (FDA-EV1MK) or optical finder (FDA-V1K) sold separately. The EVF accessory listed at $449.99 at launch (DPReview, RX1R coverage).

af.note: Contrast-detect only; slow in dim light. DPReview: about one second to focus in normal light, and 'can be very reluctant to find focus' in dim rooms. No phase detection.

body.pocket: Depth is the whole camera including the fixed lens (Sony quotes about 113.3 x 65.4 x 69.6 mm). Jacket pocket. About 15 mm deeper than a Leica CL with Summicron-C, and about the same weight.

identifiers: 'RX1R' on the front. Otherwise identical to the RX1.

viewfinder.note: None built in; FDA-EV1MK EVF or FDA-V1K optical finder optional. EVF accessory was $449.99 at launch (DPReview).

af.note: Contrast-detect only; slow in dim light. Same contrast-detect system as the RX1 (DPReview spec).

body.pocket: Same body as the RX1. Jacket pocket.

identifiers: 'RX1R II' on the front; the EVF sits in the top-left of the top plate.

viewfinder.note: Pop-up OLED EVF, 2.36M dots, 0.74x. Pops up in one motion (no push-pull like the RX100 III). Mirrorlessons: 'feels more solid' than the RX100 version.

af.note: Hybrid: 399-point phase detect plus contrast. DPReview: 'fast and accurate in most shooting situations', a bit slower than the a7R II because the whole lens unit moves.

body.pocket: Depth includes the fixed lens. Jacket pocket. About 17 mm deeper and 20 g heavier than a CL with Summicron-C.

identifiers: Built-in EVF in the top-left corner with a fixed eyecup; no pop-up.

viewfinder.note: Fixed built-in OLED EVF, 2.36M dots, 0.7x. No longer a pop-up. Reviewers call the resolution low for the price.

af.note: 693-point phase detect with AI subject recognition. Bionz XR plus AI processing unit. DPReview says Sony 'addressed the focus and battery life concerns' of the Mark II.

body.pocket: 87.5 mm includes the eyecup; lens tip to monitor is 74.5 mm (Sony via CineD). Jacket pocket, but the eyecup makes it the thickest RX1.

identifiers: Red dot on the front. The Q-P (Nov 2018) has a Leica script on the top plate instead, a quieter shutter and a revised power switch; same specs otherwise.

viewfinder.note: Built-in 3.68M-dot LCoS EVF. La Vida Leica: the EVF coating scratches easily (metal glasses frames) and cannot be replaced alone; the whole EVF unit is swapped.

af.note: Contrast-detect, fast in good light. Leica quoted 0.15 s. No phase detection.

body.pocket: Depth includes the fixed lens. Coat pocket at best. About 150 g heavier and 38 mm deeper than a CL with Summicron-C.

identifiers: Red dot, 'Q2' engraved on the top plate. Several special editions exist (not researched here).

viewfinder.note: Built-in OLED EVF, 3.68M dots, 0.76x. Same resolution as the Q but OLED, which DPReview calls a significant step up.

af.note: Contrast-detect. Leica data lists a contrast-based system. DPReview: 'solidly adequate, rather than impressive', with continuous-AF flutter.

body.pocket: Leica data sheet. Coat pocket at best. About 240 g heavier than a CL with Summicron-C.

identifiers: No red dot; 'Q2 Monochrom' markings; black chrome finish.

af.note: Contrast-detect. Same system as the Q2.

iso.note: No reviewer gave a clean-to-print number. A monochrome sensor skips demosaicing and gains about a stop over the color Q2; these figures are the guide's estimate on that basis, not a quote.

body.pocket: Weight from DPReview. Dimensions assumed same as Q2; not independently confirmed. Coat pocket at best.

identifiers: Tilting screen and a 'Q3' engraving distinguish it from the Q2.

af.note: Hybrid phase detect, contrast and depth-from-defocus; face/body detection. Firmware 4.0 (Dec 2025) reworked the UI after the SL3 and improved AF.

body.pocket: Coat pocket at best. About 250 g heavier than a CL with Summicron-C.

identifiers: Longer lens barrel with '43' and APO markings.

af.note: Hybrid phase detect with subject detection. DPReview: 'swift and responsive'; detection modes cannot start from a chosen AF point.

body.pocket: Photography Blog. Cameralabs measured 795 g with cap and hood. Coat pocket at best.

identifiers: No red badge, 'Monochrom' engraved on the top plate, pebbled leatherette (Imaging Resource).

viewfinder.note: Built-in OLED EVF, 5.76M dots. Imaging Resource: same 5.67MP-class OLED finder as the Q3.

af.note: Contrast-detect only. DPReview: unlike the color Q3 it 'does not gain phase-detection AF'. 4 fps with AF, 15 fps with AF locked.

iso.note: Too new for a reviewer consensus on noise. Leica rates it to ISO 200,000; these figures are the guide's estimate from the color Q3 plus the usual one-stop monochrome advantage, not a quote.

identifiers: Large rear screen, no card door, Zeiss logo on the front.

af.note: Contrast-detect; face detect added in firmware 1.4. DPReview: 'fairly basic' and 'occasionally unreliable', with front- and back-focus on still subjects.

body.pocket: Body 46 mm deep, 94 mm with lens (Wikipedia). Weight 837 g per Wikipedia, 800 g per DPReview. Bag camera, not a pocket camera.

identifiers: Aspect-ratio dial on the top plate, square lens hood.

af.note: Phase detect with subject recognition. DPReview: 'generally reliable' for street and portraits; tracking sometimes loses fast subjects.

body.pocket: 735 g with battery and card (Fujifilm). The square hood adds bulk (DPReview). Coat pocket at best.

identifiers: Finned heat sink across the back; 'fp' on the top.

viewfinder.note: None; LVF-11 loupe optional. EVF-11 finder was launched with the fp L and also fits the fp (not confirmed here).

body.pocket: depthWithLens is an estimate: body depth plus lens length. About 63 mm with the 26mm f/8 pancake. Jacket pocket; the body is RX1-sized, the lens is what sticks out.

viewfinder.note: Optional EVF-11, 3.68M dots, 0.83x. Sold as a $2,999 kit with the finder.

af.note: Hybrid phase detect plus contrast. Adds phase detection over the fp.

body.pocket: Estimate as for fp. Jacket pocket without the EVF; the EVF-11 adds bulk at the back.

identifiers: Seamless aluminum unibody, black or silver.

viewfinder.note: None. DPReview lists no finder as a con in bright light.

af.note: Hybrid phase detect with human and animal tracking. DPReview: 'very simple' but effective; PetaPixel: tracking 'impressively tenacious'.

body.pocket: depthWithLens is an estimate: body plus lens. The thinnest body here. DPReview notes sharp body edges. Jacket pocket.

identifiers: Sold in several colors; no EVF hump, no hot shoe contacts.

viewfinder.note: None. DPReview: screen washes out outdoors.

af.note: 779-point phase detect with subject detection. DPReview lists poor AF tracking as a con.

body.pocket: depthWithLens is an estimate with the Sigma 45. About 65 mm with the 26mm f/8, about 88 mm with the 20mm f/2.5. Jacket pocket with the pancake.

identifiers: One control dial on top; small 0.59x EVF.

af.note: Hybrid phase detect with real-time eye AF.

body.pocket: depthWithLens is an estimate: about 100-105 mm with the FE 40mm (body depth includes the grip). Coat pocket.

identifiers: Front and rear dials; 'II' on the body.

viewfinder.note: Corner EVF, 2.36M dots, 0.7x. DPReview: resolution 'feels too low'.

af.note: Phase detect with AI subject recognition. Recognizes people, animals, birds, insects, vehicles and aircraft (DPReview).

body.pocket: depthWithLens is an estimate with the FE 40mm. Coat pocket.

viewfinder.note: Corner EVF, 2.36M dots, 0.7x. DPReview: 'downright rudimentary' next to the a7R V.

af.note: Phase detect with AI subject recognition. Same AF generation as the a7C II.

body.pocket: depthWithLens is an estimate with the FE 40mm. Coat pocket.

reference.name: Leica CL with Summicron-C 40mm f/2
reference.note: Body 121 x 76 x 32 mm, 365 g (Wikipedia). depthWithLens is the guide's estimate: 32 mm body plus about 23 mm of lens, before the cap. Total about 490 g.

nearMisses.name: Leica CL (Typ 7323, digital, 2017)
nearMisses.why: Shares the name and the pocket-rangefinder idea, but it is APS-C, and Leica discontinued it in May 2022.

nearMisses.name: Ricoh GR IIIx
nearMisses.why: The only camera here that fits a jeans pocket, with the same 40mm-equivalent view as the Summicron-C, but the sensor is APS-C.

nearMisses.name: Fujifilm X100VI
nearMisses.why: Leaf shutter, hybrid finder and IBIS in a body about as deep as the CL with its lens, but APS-C.

nearMisses.name: Leica M10
nearMisses.why: The true digital rangefinder that takes Drew's Summicron-C, but 660 g and wider than a Q. See the M-mount guide.

nearMisses.name: Nikon Z5IIc
nearMisses.why: Announced this month as a Z5II with the EVF removed, at $1,399.95, shipping mid-October. At 72 mm deep and 620 g it is bigger than an a7C, so it is not a pocket camera.

picks.want: the closest thing to a digital CL, in budget
picks.why: the RX1R II is the only camera near the CL's size that also has a finder; the Q is 20 mm deeper but has Leica's controls, a better finder and macro, at the top of the budget.

picks.want: the smallest full-frame camera, full stop
picks.why: about $950 for the same lens and pocket size as the RX1R II. You give up the finder, fast autofocus and battery life.

picks.want: Leica handling and the Summilux under $3,000
picks.why: KEH had eight between $2,212 and $3,040. Check what Leica will still service before you buy.

picks.want: a finder, fast autofocus and all-day battery
picks.why: about $2,870 and $1,880 with the 40mm f/2.5, but over 100 mm deep: a coat pocket, not a jacket pocket.

picks.want: the cheapest way into full frame this small
picks.why: about $1,450 and $1,550 with a Sigma 45mm f/2.8. No finder on either, and no mechanical shutter.

picks.want: no compromises, and the budget can bend
picks.why: current bodies with modern autofocus and finders; used copies sell for $4,400 and $6,200.
about $4,000 used, a monochrome sensor behind the Summilux.

picks.want: the most image quality at any size
picks.why: medium format in a fixed-lens body, about $4,900 used, and the size of a Q.
